BiblicalUsage: Gamos is marriage and the wedding feast, and it runs from Cana to the kingdom. There was a marriage in Cana of Galilee in John 2:1, and Jesus turned the water into wine there. Marriage is honourable in all, says Hebrews 13:4, and the servants are to wait like men who wait for their lord when he returns from the wedding in Luke 12:36. The king's wedding was furnished with guests, both bad and good, in Matthew 22:10.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe marriage is God's picture of His joy, and the wedding feast is His picture of the kingdom. Cana's wine and the king's feast both point to a day when the Bridegroom comes, and I hold that the marriage supper of the Lamb is the end of every wedding.
